title: Quantum Dissipative Paraelectricity
abstract: Whether a quantum system with a double-well effective potential undergoes spontaneous symmetry breaking depends not only on the potential landscape but also on the kinetics and the coupling with additional degrees of freedom. Here we introduce a quasi-exactly solvable model to study this problem in the context of ferroelectrics, with results that apply to a broad class of quantum phase transitions. Exploiting the analytical solutions, we provide a strict definition of the quantum paraelectric regime and identify a distinct quantum ferroelectric regime in which symmetry breaking can be realized without tunneling features. We then show that explicit symmetry breaking cannot be inferred from the order-parameter Hamiltonian alone, but requires additional couplings. This leads us to identify a regime of \emph{quantum dissipative paraelectricity}, in which observable symmetry breaking is suppressed during the evolution toward the ground state, even when the double-well structure dominates over zero-point quantum fluctuations.
summary: This paper analyzes quantum phase transitions in ferroelectrics modeled by a double-well potential, showing that spontaneous symmetry breaking cannot be determined by the Hamiltonian alone. It introduces the concept of quantum dissipative paraelectricity, a regime where environmental coupling suppresses observable symmetry breaking even when the potential suggests otherwise.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether spontaneous symmetry breaking in a quantum system with a double-well potential depends solely on the potential landscape or also requires kinetic effects and coupling to an environment.
main_result: Observable symmetry breaking requires explicit coupling to an environment, leading to the identification of a 'quantum dissipative paraelectricity' regime where symmetry breaking is suppressed during ground state evolution.
method: The study employs analytical solutions for a quasi-exactly solvable model, analyzing the time evolution of the probability density under environmental coupling.
model_or_system: The system models ferroelectrics using an order parameter $u$ governed by a Razavy potential. The analysis distinguishes between quantum paraelectric, quantum ferroelectric, and tunneling ferroelectric regimes.

main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the necessity of coupling to an environment to achieve observable symmetry breaking, and it utilizes approximations regarding the time evolution of the probability density.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Razavy potential, the ground-state probability density bifurcation, and the thermal probability density across various regimes (TFE, QFE, QPE, PE), showing symmetry preservation in all cases.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the problem concerning symmetry breaking dependence, then defining the QPE and QFE regimes using analytical solutions, and finally extending the analysis to include environmental coupling to derive the concept of quantum dissipative paraelectricity.
why_interesting: The explicit inclusion of dissipation and environmental coupling to determine the conditions for symmetry breaking is highly relevant to open quantum systems, providing a framework to understand how decoherence or coupling can stabilize or suppress ordered phases.

FIG. 2. Thermal probability density ρ(x; T) in the tunneling ferroelectric (TFE), quantum ferroelectric (QFE), quantum para- electric (QPE), and standard paraelectric (PE) regimes. Within each panel, curves correspond to temperatures logarithmically equally spaced up to kBT = E3. In all cases ρ(x; T) remains symmetric, reflecting the symmetry of the equilibrium density matrix. The central density ρ(0; T) increases with temperature in the TFE panel but decreases in panel QPE, providing an observable distinction between these two ferroelectric regimes.

FIG. 3. Schematic phase diagram as a function of the con- trol parameter α and the environmental coupling strength (parametrized by τ −1 1 relative to τ −1 2 and τ −1 01 ). The stan- dard paraelectric (PE) phase is superseded by the quantum paraelectric (QPE) phase between αcl c and αq c. Below αq c in the ferroelectric region, the crossover between quantum fer- roelectric (QFE) and tunneling ferroelectric (TFE) regimes is determined by the emergence of quasi-degenerate doublets. Strong environmental coupling extends the effective paraelec- tric region by sustaining the quantum dissipative paraelectric (QDPE) phase in the presence of a bifurcated ground-state probability density.
